title: Affine Koszul Hom vanishing controls the upper localization truncation
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme], and $j:W=\bigcup_{k=1}^rD(f_k)\hookrightarrow Y$, where $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Let $C_f\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ be the object obtained by sheafifying the Koszul complex $K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] termwise and placing its term $K_q$ in cochain degree $-q$. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] and $a\in\mathbf Z$. If $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(C_f[-n],E)=0$ for every integer $n\geq a$, then the canonical restriction-adjunction unit induces an isomorphism in the derived category
$$\tau_{\geq a}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\geq a}Rj_*(E|_W).$$
Here $Rj_*$ is derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and $\tau_{\geq a}$ is standard cohomological truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. The assertion includes $r=0$, when $W=\varnothing$ and $C_f=\mathcal O_Y[0]$.

proof.text: Each $D(f_k)$ is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{f_k})$ by the localization/basic-open node, and that spectrum is quasi-compact by the basic-opens/unit-ideal node. An open cover of $W$ therefore has a finite subcover on each of its finitely many $D(f_k)$; their union is finite. This also proves quasi-compactness for $r=0$. Put $B=Rj_*(E|_W)$. By the ringed-space derived adjunction applied to the open immersion $j$, for which $Lj^*$ is exact restriction to $W$, $Rj_*$ is a right adjoint of derived restriction; let $u:E\to B$ be the unit of this adjunction, the canonical map of the item. Complete $u$ to a distinguished triangle $E\xrightarrow{u}B\to C\to E[1]$. The derived open-unit-cone node applies because $W$ is quasi-compact and $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology; it gives $C\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and $C|_W=0$. Rotate backwards and put $N=C[-1]$, obtaining $N\to E\xrightarrow{u}B\to N[1]$. Since $H^q(C[-1])=H^{q-1}(C)$ and restriction commutes with shifts, $N$ has quasi-coherent cohomology and $N|_W=0$.

The Koszul restriction-zero node gives $(C_f[m])|_W=0$ for every integer $m$. Derived adjunction for the open immersion identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(C_f[m],B)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}((C_f[m])|_W,E|_W)=0$. Here $Lj^*$ is ordinary exact restriction, since on an open subscheme the pulled-back structure sheaf is the structure sheaf itself. Shift invariance also gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C_f[m],B[-1])=0$. Fix $n\geq a$ and a map $v:C_f[-n]\to N$. Its composite into $E$ is zero by the hypothesis of the item. Apply Hom-into-triangle exactness to the rotated triangle $B[-1]\to N\to E\to B$: $v$ factors through $B[-1]$ and hence is zero. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(C_f[-n],N)=0$ for every $n\geq a$, without changing the threshold.

For every positive exponent tuple $\mathbf e=(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$, let $C_{\mathbf e}$ be the sheafified cochain Koszul object for $(f_i^{e_i})$. Prove $\operatorname{Hom}(C_{\mathbf e}[-n],N)=0$ for all $n\geq a$ by strong induction on $\sum_i(e_i-1)$. At sum zero all exponents are one, so Step 2 applies. Otherwise choose $i$ with $e_i>1$ and keep the other coordinates fixed. The coordinate multiplication triangle, with scalars $f_i^{e_i-1}$ and $f_i$, has outer objects with coordinate exponents $e_i-1$ and $1$, and middle object $C_{\mathbf e}$. Both outer tuples have smaller induction measure. Shift this triangle by $-n$. For any map from its middle object to $N$, precomposition from the first object is zero by induction; Hom-out-of-triangle exactness factors it through the third object, whose Hom to $N$ is also zero by induction. This proves the claim at the same $n$. For $r=0$ the induction measure is zero and there is no induction step.

Fix $n\geq a$ and $\varphi:\mathcal O_Y[-n]\to N$. Apply supported-augmentation vanishing to $N$ and this shift: its hypotheses hold by Step 1. It supplies an index $e\in\mathbf N$ with $\varphi\circ u_e[-n]=0$. Its convention is that index $e$ means exponent $e+1$. The represent-cohomology node supplies the triangle $I_e\xrightarrow{u_e}\mathcal O_Y\to K_e\to I_e[1]$, where $K_e=C_{(e+1,\ldots,e+1)}$. Apply Hom-out-of-triangle exactness to its shift by $-n$: $\varphi$ factors through $K_e[-n]$. Step 3 makes this factor zero, so $\varphi=0$. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_Y[-n],N)=0$ for all $n\geq a$.

Apply the structure-sheaf Hom/hypercohomology bijection to $N[n]$. Shifting the source identifies its Hom group with $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_Y[-n],N)$, zero by Step 4, so $H^0(R\Gamma(Y,N[n]))=0$. The affine derived equivalence is triangulated, hence its quasi-inverse $R\Gamma(Y,-)$ commutes with shifts; thus this is $H^n(R\Gamma(Y,N))=0$. Write $F$ for the equivalence from $D(A)$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ induced by termwise associated sheaf. Since $N$ is quasi-coherent, its counit gives $F(R\Gamma(Y,N))\simeq N$. The affine tilde/homology comparison applies to this very $F$ and gives $H^n(N)\simeq\widetilde{H^n(R\Gamma(Y,N))}=0$ for every $n\geq a$. In particular this uses the cohomology comparison, not merely conservativity of the affine equivalence.

Apply the cohomological-functor clause of the heart/triangle theorem to $N\to E\xrightarrow{u}B\to N[1]$. For each $n\geq a$ its exact segment is $H^n(N)\to H^n(E)\xrightarrow{H^n(u)}H^n(B)\to H^{n+1}(N)$. Both outside objects vanish by Step 5, since $n+1\geq a$ as well. Therefore $H^n(u)$ is an isomorphism in every degree $n\geq a$. Standard truncation keeps these cohomology objects and kills those below $a$, so $\tau_{\geq a}(u)$ induces an isomorphism in every degree.

A morphism of derived objects that induces isomorphisms on every cohomology object is invertible: use the cited calculus of quasi-isomorphisms and right-fraction representation in the homotopy category to represent it by a roof $P\xleftarrow{s}Q\xrightarrow{t}R$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Since $H^n(s)$ and the cohomology maps of the roof are invertible, $H^n(t)$ is invertible for every $n$ as well. Thus both arrows of the roof are inverted in the localization defining the derived category. Apply this to $\tau_{\geq a}(u)$ from Step 6. This proves the claimed isomorphism for the canonical unit itself.

tool_uses.why: Topological localization identifies each principal open with a spectrum; a generic tool establishing the compact-open hypothesis.
Quasi-compactness of a ring spectrum, used on each localization; the unit has no corresponding structure-sheaf tool.
The generic structure-sheaf localization cone is quasi-coherent and supported; no finite-coefficient or pro-etale operation is substituted.
The actual sheafified Koszul complex vanishes on its union of principal opens.
Unbounded module-sheaf derived adjunction, applied only to the Zariski open immersion.
Generic covariant representable exactness for the supported fibre.
Generic multiplication triangle; the bounded-range power induction is written in Step 3 rather than using the all-shifts orthogonality theorem.
Generic contravariant representable exactness for power induction and augmentation factorization.
Generic supported-object augmentation vanishing, which makes each structure-sheaf morphism factor through a power Koszul object.
Only its stated augmentation triangle is used to factor a map after the tail augmentation becomes zero.
Generic structure-sheaf Hom equals hypercohomology, applied to the shifted supported object.
The unbounded affine quasi-coherent equivalence supplies the counit and shift compatibility.
Degreewise cohomology comparison for the existing termwise-tilde equivalence; needed beyond bare equivalence.
Generic cohomology long exact sequence, clause (5), with no boundedness requirement.
Generic homotopy-category calculus of quasi-isomorphisms, needed for the elementary final inversion argument.
Generic localization roof representation, applied to the actual homotopy category of module sheaves.
